classification.difficultyReason: Prove similarity from parallel lines, calculate a length using corresponding sides, and identify additional similar triangles.

spec.description: Unshaded parallelogram ABCD with DC extended to E and AE intersecting BC at F. Double arrows identify AD parallel to BC; single arrows identify AB parallel to DC. Ordinary source blue strokes are reconstructed in house black.
spec.mathematics: AD ∥ BC; AB ∥ DC; A,F,E collinear; D,C,E collinear.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied geometry and labels remain visible; no answers are shown.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Prove that $\triangle AFB$ is similar to $\triangle EFC$.

answer.short: $\triangle AFB\sim\triangle EFC$ (AAA), using vertically opposite angles and alternate angles.
answer.worked:
$\angle AFB=\angle EFC$ (vertically opposite angles).

$\angle ABF=\angle ECF$ (alternate angles, $AB\parallel CE$).

The remaining angles are equal because each triangle has angle sum $180^\circ$.

Therefore $\triangle AFB\sim\triangle EFC$ (AAA).

children.label: b
children.prompt: Given that $AD=10\text{ cm}$, $CD=4\text{ cm}$ and $CE=1\text{ cm}$, calculate $FC$.

answer.worked:
$ABCD$ is a parallelogram, so $AB=CD=4\text{ cm}$ and $BC=AD=10\text{ cm}$.

Using corresponding sides of the similar triangles from part a,
$$\begin{align*}\frac{BF}{FC}&=\frac{AB}{EC}\\\frac{BF}{FC}&=\frac{4}{1}\\BF&=4FC.\end{align*}$$
Since $BF+FC=BC$,
$$\begin{align*}4FC+FC&=10\\5FC&=10\\FC&=2\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Name two other pairs of similar triangles.

answer.worked:
$\triangle DAE\sim\triangle CFE$ (AAA): $\angle DEA=\angle CEF$ is common, and $\angle DAE=\angle CFE$ because $AD\parallel CF$.

$\triangle DAE\sim\triangle BFA$ (AAA): $\angle DAE=\angle BFA$ because $AD\parallel BF$, and $\angle DEA=\angle BAF$ because $DE\parallel BA$. In each pair the third angles are also equal.
